problem: EQA agents pre-trained on fixed environments fail when deployed in unseen environments (e.g. different people's houses), and re-training in each new environment is costly.
motivation: Real-world agents constantly face unseen environments, so they need to keep learning on their own without expensive re-training. The paper proposes continual, self-supervised adaptation to handle this.
key_idea: Use generative adversarial imitation learning with self-supervision for continual adaptation of an EQA agent, with a policy generator that produces action sequences and a policy quality discriminator that scores them.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablations or analyses can be reported. The abstract suggests that adversarial imitation of policy quality can serve as a self-supervised signal for adapting to unseen environments without labels.
method: Policy generator: generates action policy sequences for navigation in the EQA task.
Policy quality discriminator: evaluates the quality of the generated policy sequences, in an adversarial (GAIL-style) setup.
Continual learning with self-supervision: the agent adapts to unseen environments by itself without full re-training.
